newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks extend losses in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks extend losses in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange extended this week's gentle slide on Tuesday, slipping 0.07 percent in quiet trade dominated by private transactions in banking shares, brokers said.
"Turnover's weak and there are no signs of an upturn in the near future," said one dealer.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share fell 0.11 points to 148.36 points on Tuesday in turnover worth 578,000 dinars. The index has fallen daily since Saturday's close of 148.75 points.

Brokers say stalemate in Palestinian-Israeli talks and growing consensus that neighbouring Iraq will not export even limited quantities of oil before next year have both weighed heavily on a market already short of cash and cramped by poor domestic investor sentiment.

Jordan Gulf Bank closed unchanged at 0.91 dinars after accounting for a third of Monday's turnover, but brokers said the volume came mainly from a single block deal at 0.89 dinars. Arab Bank Group, which rose 0.25 dinars to 247 dinars, and The Housing Bank, which closed unchanged at 4.80 dinars, also registered healthy turnover.
"If you take away the block trades, today's turnover was less than 300,000 dinars," said one broker.
Declining shares outnumber rising stock by 23 to seven on Tuesday, with eight trading but closing unchanged.
